event_overview.title: About the 2026 FIFA World Cup
event_overview.subject: FIFA World Cup
event_overview.summary: The FIFA World Cup is FIFA’s flagship men’s national-team football tournament. In this context, it refers to the 2026 final competition, staged across Canada, Mexico and the United States, while the selected timeline focuses on post-tournament governance and commercial questions rather than on-field results.

facts.label: Dates
facts.value: The 2026 final competition ran from 11 June to 19 July 2026; the final was scheduled for New York New Jersey Stadium.

facts.label: Hosts and footprint
facts.value: Canada, Mexico and the United States co-hosted the tournament, with matches held across 16 host cities.

facts.label: Governing body
facts.value: FIFA governs the competition. FIFA’s statutes identify the FIFA World Cup as a FIFA competition and provide that its host is decided by the FIFA Congress.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers late-July 2026 debate over FIFA’s reported investment and commercial plans; it does not provide a match-by-match account of the tournament or a full history of the World Cup.

event_overview.title: About Iran War
event_overview.subject: Iran War
event_overview.summary: The Iran War is an ongoing armed conflict that began on February 28, 2026, when the United States and Israel carried out strikes in Iran and Iran subsequently attacked U.S. military assets and regional states. It has expanded beyond direct military exchanges to include disputes over maritime access in the Strait of Hormuz, ceasefire efforts, and risks to commercial shipping and civilian seafarers.

facts.label: Start and principal belligerents
facts.value: The United Nations reported that U.S. and Israeli strikes against Iran occurred on February 28, 2026; Iran then targeted U.S. military assets and attacks affected several regional states. In a subsequent Security Council letter, the United States said it had commenced combat operations against Iran that day in cooperation with Israel.

facts.label: Geographic focus
facts.value: A central theater is the Strait of Hormuz, the waterway between Iran and Oman linking the Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman. The conflict has also affected U.S. forces and states across the Gulf region.

facts.label: Maritime and legal dimension
facts.value: The International Maritime Organization has treated attacks on merchant shipping and restrictions on passage through Hormuz as a major international-shipping issue. Its Council stated that transit passage through straits used for international navigation must not be threatened, impeded, denied, or suspended, and that any traffic measures must accord with IMO rules and international law.

facts.label: Diplomatic framework
facts.value: Ceasefire and mediation efforts have occurred alongside renewed fighting. The UN described a June 17 memorandum of understanding and Qatar-facilitated implementation talks, while warning in early July that the arrangement remained fragile after further U.S.-Iran confrontations.

facts.label: Civilian shipping impact
facts.value: IMO said on June 15 that it had verified at least 46 attacks on international shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz since the conflict began, and it later organized a voluntary emergency framework to help vessels and seafarers confined in the Gulf depart safely.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the late-July 2026 escalation involving U.S. threats and strikes, congressional war-powers action, Houthi-linked developments, oil-market disruption, and a reported pause in attacks; it does not provide a complete record of the war’s origins, all regional operations, or the full course of diplomacy.

event_overview.title: About Migration Crisis
event_overview.subject: Migration Crisis
event_overview.summary: This event concerns an episode of heightened irregular crossings into Ceuta, the Spanish autonomous city on the North African coast that borders Morocco. Such episodes sit within the wider Western Mediterranean migration route, where border management, access to asylum procedures, bilateral Spain–Morocco cooperation, and the safety of people attempting crossings are recurring issues.

facts.label: Location and status
facts.value: Ceuta is a Spanish autonomous city; its autonomy is governed by Organic Law 1/1995. Its land boundary with Morocco is an external border of the Schengen area.

facts.label: Migration-route context
facts.value: The EU describes the Western Mediterranean route as irregular arrivals to Spain by sea and by land through Ceuta and Melilla; people commonly transit through Morocco or Algeria on this route.

facts.label: Asylum access
facts.value: People may request asylum at Spain’s land borders in Ceuta and Melilla. The border procedure includes an interview by police and access to legal assistance and interpretation.

facts.label: Legal framework
facts.value: Spain is party to the 1951 Refugee Convention and its 1967 Protocol, and its domestic international-protection framework includes Law 12/2009.

facts.label: Long-running character
facts.value: Large and dangerous attempts to enter Ceuta from Morocco are not new: UNHCR documented increased mass attempts at the Ceuta and Melilla fences in 2005, illustrating the recurring nature of pressure at these border crossings.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the late-July 2026 Ceuta surge and official responses; it does not attempt to cover all migration to Spain, all Spain–Morocco relations, or the full history of the Western Mediterranean route.

event_overview.title: About Ukraine Conflict
event_overview.subject: Ukraine Conflict
event_overview.summary: The Ukraine conflict is the ongoing interstate war centered on Russia’s military actions against Ukraine, including the full-scale invasion launched on February 24, 2022, against a backdrop of Russia’s actions in and against Ukraine since 2014. It has involved sustained combat, long-range missile and drone attacks, humanitarian disruption, and international diplomatic, legal, and sanctions responses.

facts.label: Conflict timeline
facts.value: Russia’s full-scale invasion began on February 24, 2022; international institutions also treat the wider situation as encompassing events in Ukraine from 2013-14 onward.

facts.label: Location and parties
facts.value: The conflict is fought primarily on and over Ukraine’s internationally recognized territory, involving Russia and Ukraine; the UN General Assembly has repeatedly reaffirmed Ukraine’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity within those borders.

facts.label: International legal position
facts.value: The UN General Assembly’s March 2, 2022 resolution characterized Russia’s actions as aggression against Ukraine and demanded that Russia end its use of force and withdraw its military forces.

facts.label: International criminal investigation
facts.value: The International Criminal Court opened its Ukraine investigation on March 2, 2022. Its stated scope covers alleged war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide committed by any person on any part of Ukraine’s territory from November 21, 2013 onward.

facts.label: Humanitarian dimension
facts.value: The war has produced a major humanitarian and displacement emergency; UNHCR describes the February 2022 escalation as one of the fastest-growing displacement emergencies in recent history.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline follows major late-July and early-August 2026 military, diplomatic and cross-border developments connected to the war; it does not attempt to provide a complete account of the conflict’s battlefield, humanitarian, political or legal history.

event_overview.title: About Mountaineering Incident
event_overview.subject: Mountaineering Incident
event_overview.summary: This event is a fatal avalanche involving a 10-person mountaineering expedition on Broad Peak in Pakistan’s Karakoram range. The avalanche struck on July 30, 2026, during an ascent attempt; after search operations were constrained by severe conditions, the expedition company confirmed that all 10 climbers had died.

facts.label: Date and outcome
facts.value: The avalanche occurred on July 30, 2026. By August 1, the expedition company had confirmed the deaths of all 10 members of the group.

facts.label: Location
facts.value: Broad Peak is an 8,047-metre mountain in the Karakoram on the Pakistan–China border, in the Gilgit-Baltistan region of Pakistan.

facts.label: Expedition
facts.value: The affected party was a 10-member climbing expedition attempting to summit Broad Peak; Nirmal Purja was identified in reporting as its leader.

facts.label: Search and recovery
facts.value: Rescuers initially located four bodies and recovered three, while harsh weather impeded helicopter-supported search and recovery operations.

facts.label: Protected-area context
facts.value: Broad Peak is among the mountains within Central Karakoram National Park, a Gilgit-Baltistan protected area established in 1993.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the initial reports of climbers missing, the reported death toll, and subsequent confirmation of all 10 deaths; it does not provide a complete account of recovery operations, the avalanche’s cause, or wider climbing-season developments.

event_overview.title: About Wildfires
event_overview.subject: Wildfires
event_overview.summary: This event concerns a late-July 2026 wildfire emergency affecting parts of France and Spain, where fire weather, vegetation conditions and threats to populated areas prompted protective measures including evacuations. It sits within a wider European wildfire-risk context in which national civil-protection authorities lead local response while EU systems provide monitoring, forecasting and, when requested, cross-border assistance.

facts.label: Timeframe
facts.value: The selected developments cover July 25-28, 2026, during the main summer wildfire period in southwestern Europe.

facts.label: Countries and response authorities
facts.value: Wildfire response is principally organized by national and subnational civil-protection, fire and forest services. In Spain, the Interior Ministry declared an emergency of national interest for fires affecting Madrid and Ávila and later extended it to Toledo; it also requested activation of the EU Civil Protection Mechanism.

facts.label: Wildfire-risk conditions
facts.value: Wildfire behavior is strongly affected by temperature, humidity, wind and precipitation. France’s government says higher temperatures and drier vegetation associated with climate change are intensifying and expanding wildfire risk, while the EU’s fire-danger assessments indicated extreme to very extreme conditions across parts of France and the Iberian Peninsula in early July 2026.

facts.label: European monitoring
facts.value: The European Forest Fire Information System (EFFIS), part of Copernicus Emergency Management Service, provides near-real-time and historical fire information, including danger assessment, active-fire and burned-area mapping, damage assessment, emissions and smoke-dispersion information. It was established by the European Commission with national fire administrations and supports national services and the EU Emergency

facts.label: Prevention and public safety
facts.value: France treats forest and vegetation fires as a major natural-risk issue and uses prevention planning, vegetation-clearing obligations in designated risk areas, public alerts and civil-protection guidance. Spain’s 2026 planning framework likewise emphasizes coordinated civil-protection plans, alerting and public information during wildfire emergencies.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline follows the late-July 2026 France-and-Spain evacuation crisis and associated official actions; it does not aim to provide a complete incident log, independently settle displacement totals, or catalogue every fire perimeter, weather alert or firefighting deployment.

event_overview.subject: Japan Earthquake
event_overview.summary: A magnitude 7.1 earthquake struck the Kumamoto area of Kyushu, southwestern Japan, on July 28, 2026, causing fatalities, injuries and structural damage. The disaster response includes searches for people affected by collapses and monitoring of continued seismic activity, while authorities assess localized tsunami risk and issue public warnings as needed.

facts.label: Date and location
facts.value: The main earthquake occurred on July 28, 2026, in the Kumamoto area of Kyushu, Japan’s southwestern main island.

facts.label: Magnitude and impacts
facts.value: Initial reporting described the earthquake as magnitude 7.1, with destructive shaking that damaged buildings and infrastructure and led to casualties.

facts.label: Earthquake and tsunami authority
facts.value: Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) is the national authority that rapidly determines an earthquake’s location, magnitude and observed intensity, and distributes earthquake information to disaster-prevention authorities and the public.

facts.label: Tsunami alerts
facts.value: When a quake may produce damaging coastal waves, JMA issues tsunami warnings or advisories by forecast region, generally within about two to three minutes; advisories call for people to leave the water and coast until they are lifted.

facts.label: Seismic-intensity system
facts.value: Japan reports local shaking separately from magnitude using JMA’s 10-level seismic-intensity scale, which reflects ground motion at a particular place and can vary with distance and local geology.

event_overview.scope_note: This timeline follows the July 28–29, 2026 Kumamoto-area earthquake, including rescue operations, aftershocks and tsunami alerts; it does not attempt to cover all earthquakes in Japan or every subsequent damage assessment and emergency update.

event_overview.title: About COVID-19 Hearing
event_overview.subject: COVID-19 Hearing
event_overview.summary: This was a U.S. Senate oversight hearing featuring former National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases director Anthony Fauci, held by the Senate Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs (HSGAC). It occurred in the context of the committee’s continuing examination of federal handling of COVID-19 origins, related research, and government transparency; the selected timeline focuses on the immediate dispute over testimony and possible congressional enforcement rather than resolving the pandemic’s origin.

facts.label: Date and venue
facts.value: The full-committee hearing, listed as “Testimony of Anthony Fauci,” was held on July 29, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. in room SD-342 of the Senate Dirksen Building.

facts.label: Witness
facts.value: The hearing’s sole listed witness was Anthony Fauci, M.D., identified by the committee as former director of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, a position he held from 1984 to 2022, within the National Institutes of Health and Department of Health and Human Services.

facts.label: Subject context
facts.value: In a May 2026 HSGAC hearing on COVID-19 and gain-of-function research, the committee framed its inquiry around the origins of COVID-19, intelligence-community transparency, potential conflicts involving outside scientific advisers, and federal research oversight. Those are the surrounding issues for the later Fauci testimony, not findings established by the hearing itself.

facts.label: Congressional-enforcement framework
facts.value: Federal law provides that a person summoned by either chamber or a committee who willfully defaults or refuses to answer a question pertinent to the inquiry may face criminal contempt of Congress; under 2 U.S.C. § 194, a contempt matter may be certified to the appropriate U.S. attorney. Whether a particular assertion of the Fifth Amendment supports contempt is a fact- and law-specific question.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the July 29–31, 2026 testimony dispute and ensuing contempt discussion, not the full history of COVID-19 origins investigations, Fauci’s career, or all Senate pandemic hearings.

event_overview.title: About Ceuta Border Crisis
event_overview.subject: Ceuta Border Crisis
event_overview.summary: The Ceuta border crisis refers to acute episodes of irregular migrant arrivals from Morocco into Ceuta, a Spanish autonomous city on North Africa’s Mediterranean coast, and the resulting border-security, humanitarian and diplomatic pressures. It is closely tied to Spain-Morocco cooperation on migration management, while also raising questions about access to asylum procedures and the legality of border returns. A major precedent occurred in May 2021, when roughly 9,000 people entered Ceuta by land or sea over several days.

facts.label: Location and EU border status
facts.value: Ceuta is Spanish territory in North Africa; its border with Morocco is an external border of the Schengen area, although special identity and document checks apply when travelling onward from Ceuta to mainland Spain or other Schengen countries.

facts.label: Major earlier crisis
facts.value: The European Parliament recorded that, beginning on May 17, 2021, nearly 9,000 people entered Ceuta by swimming or walking during an exceptional surge; the episode remains a central reference point for later Ceuta border alerts.

facts.label: Spanish legal framework
facts.value: Spain’s Organic Law 4/2015 created a special Ceuta-and-Melilla border regime allowing people detected while attempting to cross border-containment structures irregularly to be refused entry, while requiring compliance with international human-rights and international-protection rules and providing for asylum applications at designated border posts.

facts.label: Judicial context
facts.value: In N.D. and N.T. v. Spain, decided by the European Court of Human Rights Grand Chamber on February 13, 2020, the Court found no violation in the immediate return to Morocco of two men who had attempted an unauthorized mass crossing of the Melilla fences; the ruling concerned that case’s particular circumstances.

facts.label: Bilateral cooperation

event_overview.title: About Middle East Conflict
event_overview.subject: Middle East Conflict
event_overview.summary: This event concerns the risk that attacks by Yemen’s Houthi movement (Ansar Allah) on Saudi-linked oil shipping or energy infrastructure could widen the Yemen and Red Sea security crisis and disrupt oil flows. It sits within the longer Yemen conflict, in which Houthi forces took Sana’a in 2014 and Saudi Arabia led a military coalition from 2015, alongside a separate pattern of Houthi attacks on commercial navigation in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden.

facts.label: Origins of the Yemen conflict
facts.value: Houthi forces captured Yemen’s capital, Sana’a, in September 2014; the UN Security Council records that they then sought in January 2015 to replace the government with a Houthi-dominated authority.

facts.label: Saudi Arabia’s role
facts.value: Saudi Arabia formed and led a coalition that began military operations in Yemen in March 2015 after Yemen’s president requested external support; the conflict subsequently included Houthi cross-border missile, drone and rocket attacks on Saudi territory.

facts.label: Relevant waterways
facts.value: The maritime dimension centers on the Red Sea, the Bab al-Mandab strait and the Gulf of Aden—routes used by merchant vessels moving between the Suez Canal and the Indian Ocean.

facts.label: International legal and diplomatic frame
facts.value: UN Security Council Resolution 2216 (2015) demanded that the Houthis end violence, withdraw from seized areas and refrain from threats or provocations against neighboring states; Resolution 2722 (2024) demanded an immediate end to Houthi attacks on merchant and commercial vessels in the Red Sea.

facts.label: Ceasefire context
facts.value: A UN-brokered Yemen truce began on April 2, 2022 and formally expired on October 2, 2022. The UN says the overall front-line military situation remained comparatively stable afterward, while its Special Envoy continued pursuing a nationwide ceasefire and Yemeni-led political settlement.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the July 2026 escalation involving alleged Houthi attacks, oil-price concerns and related U.S.-Iran diplomacy; it does not attempt to chronicle the full Yemen war, every Red Sea incident, or all regional negotiations.

event_overview.title: About Youth Protests
event_overview.subject: Youth Protests
event_overview.summary: Youth-led demonstrations in India grew around alleged irregularities in the 2026 National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test for undergraduate medical education (NEET-UG), including claims of a leaked paper and the disruption caused by a nationwide re-examination. The protests, centered visibly in New Delhi but supported more broadly, expanded into demands for accountability, examination-system reforms, and the education minister’s departure.

facts.label: Examination and re-test dates
facts.value: NTA scheduled NEET-UG 2026 for May 3, 2026; its official notices show that a re-examination was conducted on June 21, 2026.

facts.label: Examination purpose
facts.value: NEET-UG is the common, uniform entrance test for undergraduate medical education in India; it also applies to specified undergraduate Indian-system-of-medicine and homeopathy courses.

facts.label: Exam administrator
facts.value: The National Testing Agency (NTA), an autonomous organization under India’s Ministry of Education’s Department of Higher Education, administers NEET-UG and other national entrance examinations.

facts.label: Protest setting and stated demands
facts.value: The movement’s most visible sit-in site was Jantar Mantar in central New Delhi. Organizers sought the education minister’s resignation, examination reforms, and compensation for families of students reported to have died by suicide after exam irregularities.

facts.label: Legal context
facts.value: India’s Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024, in force from June 21, 2024, covers paper or answer-key leaks and related collusion among prohibited unfair means in covered public examinations.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline focuses on the youth mobilization and ministerial-resignation developments of July 25, 2026, rather than providing a complete account of the NEET investigation, re-examination administration, court process, or all related education-policy disputes.

event_overview.title: About Iran Conflict
event_overview.subject: Iran Conflict
event_overview.summary: The Iran Conflict refers here to the 2026 direct military confrontation between the United States and Iran, which has expanded beyond Iranian territory to include attacks and claimed attacks on U.S. forces, partner states and maritime activity in the Middle East. The confrontation has centered in part on control and security of the Strait of Hormuz, while Iran’s reported retaliatory operations have involved missiles and drones directed at regional sites hosting U.S. personnel.

facts.label: Start of the direct conflict
facts.value: Reporting describes U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran on February 28, 2026, as the start of the present direct war; it is distinct from the longer-running U.S.-Iran rivalry and regional proxy conflicts.

facts.label: Ceasefire and renewed fighting
facts.value: The United States and Iran reached an interim arrangement or ceasefire in mid-June 2026, but reporting says the truce subsequently broke down amid a confrontation over the Strait of Hormuz and renewed U.S. and Iranian attacks.

facts.label: Geographic scope
facts.value: The conflict’s military and economic effects extend across Iran, the Strait of Hormuz and neighboring states that host U.S. facilities, including Bahrain, Kuwait and Jordan; reports of individual strikes and damage may be contested or unverified.

facts.label: Why Bahrain and Kuwait matter
facts.value: Bahrain hosts U.S. Naval Support Activity Bahrain and the U.S. Fifth Fleet/NAVCENT presence, while Camp Arifjan in Kuwait supports Army prepositioned stocks and theater sustainment for U.S. Central Command operations.

facts.label: Maritime dimension
facts.value: The Strait of Hormuz is a central theater because it is a strategic shipping chokepoint; the U.S. Fifth Fleet’s area of responsibility includes the Arabian Gulf and the strait, alongside other regional waterways.

event_overview.title: About Israeli-Palestinian Conflict
event_overview.subject: Israeli-Palestinian Conflict
event_overview.summary: This is a localized deadly episode in the West Bank within the broader Israeli-Palestinian conflict, involving Palestinians, Israeli settlers and Israeli security authorities. Such incidents occur amid unresolved disputes over territory, security, settlements, Palestinian self-determination and the status of Jerusalem.

facts.label: Modern conflict timeline
facts.value: The question of Palestine was brought to the United Nations in 1947; the UN proposed partition that year, Israel declared independence on 14 May 1948, and Israel occupied the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, and Gaza during the June 1967 war.

facts.label: Location and territorial framework
facts.value: The West Bank, including East Jerusalem, is central to the conflict. In its 19 July 2024 advisory opinion, the International Court of Justice described the Palestinian territory occupied since 1967 as encompassing the West Bank, East Jerusalem and the Gaza Strip, treated as a single territorial unit for the opinion’s legal analysis.

facts.label: Political parties and interim governance
facts.value: Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organization signed the 13 September 1993 Declaration of Principles, which envisioned a Palestinian interim self-government authority in the West Bank and Gaza and negotiations on permanent-status issues including Jerusalem, refugees, settlements, security and borders.

facts.label: Settlements and international diplomacy
facts.value: UN Security Council resolution 2334 (2016) states that Israeli settlement activity in the Palestinian territory occupied since 1967, including East Jerusalem, has no legal validity and is a major obstacle to a two-state solution; the resolution calls for settlement activity to cease.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline follows the immediate aftermath of this July 2026 West Bank violence—funerals and subsequent detentions—but does not attempt to provide a complete account of the conflict, its casualty history or all related political and military developments.

event_overview.title: About Iran War
event_overview.subject: Iran War
event_overview.summary: The Iran War is the 2026 armed conflict involving U.S. and Israeli military operations against Iran and Iranian retaliatory attacks on U.S. and regional targets. It began with large-scale strikes on February 28, 2026, expanded into a regional security and maritime crisis, and has continued despite ceasefire and diplomatic efforts.

facts.label: Start and parties
facts.value: The current conflict began on February 28, 2026, when the United States and Israel carried out major strikes in Iran; Iran subsequently announced attacks on U.S. military assets in the region.

facts.label: U.S. operation
facts.value: U.S. Central Command says it commenced Operation Epic Fury at the President's direction at 1:15 a.m. on February 28, 2026, describing its stated aim as dismantling Iran's security apparatus and prioritizing locations it considers imminent threats.

facts.label: Regional scope
facts.value: The conflict has affected Iran and neighboring states across the Gulf and Middle East; the UN reported Iranian attacks or reported impacts involving Bahrain, Iraq, Jordan, Kuwait, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates.

facts.label: Strait of Hormuz and shipping
facts.value: The Strait of Hormuz has become a central theater because it is a strategically important Gulf shipping route. CENTCOM said it began blocking maritime traffic entering and leaving Iranian ports on April 13, while the UN has warned that maritime incidents and threats to navigation heighten escalation risks.

facts.label: Diplomacy and legal context
facts.value: The UN has urged de-escalation, respect for the UN Charter and international humanitarian law. It reported that Qatar-mediated talks sought to implement a June 17 memorandum of understanding, but renewed strikes and counterstrikes underscored the fragility of those arrangements.

event_overview.scope_note: This Muninn timeline tracks selected July 2026 U.S.-Iran military and Strait of Hormuz developments; it does not attempt to catalog all strikes, casualties, diplomatic exchanges, or regional consequences of the wider war.

The attack is being treated as an assault on the LGBTQ+ community, prompting condemnation from officials.

event_overview.title: About Berlin Pride Attack
event_overview.subject: Berlin Pride Attack
event_overview.summary: The Berlin Pride attack refers to a deadly assault in the Tiergarten area of central Berlin on July 25, 2026, during the city’s Christopher Street Day (CSD) weekend. Berlin prosecutors said the suspected attacker allegedly used a rented vehicle and a bladed weapon against people near the event; one woman died and multiple people were injured, with the investigation continuing.

facts.label: Date and location
facts.value: Authorities place the attack at about 10 p.m. on July 25, 2026, in the Tiergarten area of Berlin, in the vicinity of Christopher Street Day celebrations.

facts.label: Alleged method and casualties
facts.value: The Berlin General Prosecutor’s Office said the suspect was alleged to have injured several people with a rented vehicle and a bladed weapon; a woman died that evening and other people were seriously injured.

facts.label: Underlying event
facts.value: Berlin CSD 2026 was the 48th Berlin Christopher Street Day, organized by Berliner CSD e.V.; organizers described it as a demonstration for democracy, diversity and human rights.

facts.label: CSD schedule and format
facts.value: The Pride weekend was scheduled for July 24-25, 2026. Its July 25 demonstration was to begin on Leipziger Straße, proceed via Potsdamer Platz and Nollendorfplatz toward the Victory Column, with programming around the Brandenburg Gate.

facts.label: Investigation
facts.value: The Berlin General Prosecutor’s Office and police described the case as an active investigation and said that detailed public disclosures were limited in order to protect it.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the immediate attack and law-enforcement response on July 26-27, 2026; it does not provide a full account of the broader Berlin CSD program, later legal proceedings, or longer-term security and policy consequences.

facts.label: Prior public reporting and denial
facts.value: The July 2026 documentary followed a June 7, 2025 Air Mail report in which nine women accused Leto of impropriety; his representative denied those earlier allegations, and Leto personally denied the later allegations to AP.

event_overview.title: About Tate Brothers Arrest
event_overview.subject: Tate Brothers Arrest
event_overview.summary: The event concerns the July 2026 U.S. arrest of Andrew and Tristan Tate after UK prosecutors sought their extradition to face criminal charges in England. It is an extradition and charging matter, not a finding of guilt: the Crown Prosecution Service says the proceedings are active and that guilt can be determined only by a court.

facts.label: Arrest and location
facts.value: The brothers were arrested by the U.S. Marshals Service in the United States on July 18, 2026; reporting and the selected timeline identify Miami, Florida, as the location of the arrest.

facts.label: UK charging scope
facts.value: The CPS said it would pursue extradition on 21 pre-existing charges and further charges involving four additional alleged victims. The added allegations include rape, arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation, assault, and offences relating to indecent images of a child and extreme pornography.

facts.label: Alleged time period and victims
facts.value: According to the CPS, the further alleged offending occurred between July 2010 and August 2017; the charging decisions brought the stated total number of alleged victims in the UK case to seven.

facts.label: Earlier extradition history
facts.value: UK extradition warrants were issued at Westminster Magistrates’ Court in January 2024. In March 2024, the Bucharest Court of Appeal ordered extradition to the UK only after separate Romanian criminal proceedings concluded.

facts.label: Legal status
facts.value: The CPS requested extradition from the United States, and as of July 19, 2026 said the brothers had been arrested and were awaiting extradition proceedings. The CPS emphasizes that a charging decision is not a finding of fact or guilt and that the defendants have a right to a fair trial.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the Miami arrest and the initial U.S. extradition challenge from July 19–21, 2026, rather than the underlying evidence, the separate Romanian proceedings, or any eventual extradition or trial outcome.

event_overview.title: About US-Saudi Nuclear Deal
event_overview.subject: US-Saudi Nuclear Deal
event_overview.summary: The event concerns a U.S.-Saudi agreement for peaceful nuclear cooperation, commonly called a “123 agreement,” signed on July 22, 2026 alongside a bilateral safeguards agreement. It establishes a legal framework for potential U.S. civil-nuclear exports and commercial participation in Saudi Arabia’s nuclear-energy program, while making nonproliferation, safety and security central stated objectives.

facts.label: Parties and date
facts.value: U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright and Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman signed the peaceful nuclear cooperation agreement and an accompanying bilateral safeguards agreement on July 22, 2026.

facts.label: Legal framework
facts.value: The accord is a Section 123 agreement under the U.S. Atomic Energy Act of 1954—the mechanism used for significant civil nuclear cooperation, including NRC-licensed exports of nuclear material, reactors, equipment and components.

facts.label: Congressional process
facts.value: The Department of Energy said the agreement would be transmitted to Congress for review; standard Section 123 agreements are subject to two review periods totaling 90 days of continuous congressional session before they may enter into force absent enacted disapproval.

facts.label: Stated purpose
facts.value: DOE describes the arrangement as supporting U.S. access to Saudi nuclear-energy opportunities and Saudi energy needs, while advancing nuclear safety, security and nonproliferation objectives.

facts.label: International safeguards context
facts.value: Saudi Arabia’s comprehensive safeguards agreement with the International Atomic Energy Agency has been in force since January 13, 2009; its Small Quantities Protocol was rescinded effective December 31, 2024.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the July 22–23, 2026 approval/signing and finalization developments, not the subsequent congressional review, implementation, specific export licenses, commercial contracts, or construction of any Saudi nuclear facilities.

event_overview.title: About Brazil Elections
event_overview.subject: Brazil Elections
event_overview.summary: Brazil’s 2026 general elections will choose the country’s president and vice president alongside governors, senators, and federal and state or district legislators. The presidential contest is a nationwide direct election administered by Brazil’s Electoral Justice, with a second round if no ticket wins an absolute majority of valid votes in the first round.

facts.label: Election dates
facts.value: The first round is scheduled for October 4, 2026; a second round, where required, is scheduled for October 25, 2026.

facts.label: Offices being elected
facts.value: Voters will elect the president and vice president, state and Federal District governors and vice governors, senators, federal deputies, and state or district deputies; two Senate seats are being contested in each state and the Federal District in this cycle.

facts.label: Electoral system for president
facts.value: The president and vice president run as a single ticket. A ticket must receive an absolute majority of valid votes to win in the first round; otherwise, the two leading tickets proceed to a runoff.

facts.label: Candidate selection and registration
facts.value: Political parties and federations may hold conventions from July 20 through August 5, 2026 to choose candidates and decide coalitions. A public campaign launch is distinct from the formal registration process; presidential and vice-presidential registration requests are decided by the Superior Electoral Court (TSE).

facts.label: Election administration
facts.value: The Superior Electoral Court’s 2026 rules govern preparation, voting, vote counting, tabulation, certification of winners, and post-election procedures for the general election.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline follows specific developments involving a presidential campaign and Brazil–Argentina diplomatic tensions, rather than providing a complete record of candidates, court rulings, polling, campaign activity, or election results.

event_overview.title: About UK Prime Minister Transition
event_overview.subject: UK Prime Minister Transition
event_overview.summary: This event is the July 2026 transfer of leadership of the UK government from Keir Starmer to Andy Burnham after Starmer resigned and Burnham became Labour leader. Burnham formally took office on 20 July 2026, when he accepted King Charles III’s invitation to form a government; reports dated 21 July cover his first full day in office rather than a separate constitutional swearing-in.

facts.label: Effective date
facts.value: Andy Burnham became Prime Minister on 20 July 2026; the UK Parliament records his premiership as beginning that day.

facts.label: Transfer of office
facts.value: Keir Starmer said he was resigning on 20 July 2026, and Burnham stated that he had accepted the King’s invitation at Buckingham Palace to form a government.

facts.label: Constitutional basis
facts.value: The prime minister is head of the UK government and holds office by being able to command the confidence of the House of Commons; political parties determine and communicate who is best placed to do so, after which the Sovereign appoints the successor.

facts.label: Political and parliamentary position
facts.value: Burnham was elected Labour leader in July 2026 and is the Labour MP for Makerfield, elected in June 2026.

facts.label: Office and responsibilities
facts.value: As prime minister, Burnham is also First Lord of the Treasury, Minister for the Civil Service and Minister for the Union; the prime minister leads His Majesty’s Government and is ultimately responsible for government policy and decisions.

event_overview.title: About Tropical Storms
event_overview.subject: Tropical Storms
event_overview.summary: This tracked event concerns concurrent tropical cyclones affecting two U.S. National Hurricane Center monitoring areas: Bertha in the Atlantic basin, including the Gulf Coast, and Fausto in the eastern North Pacific. Tropical storms are named tropical cyclones with sustained winds of 39–73 mph; once sustained winds reach 74 mph, they are classified as hurricanes.

facts.label: Seasonal timing
facts.value: The Atlantic hurricane season, which includes the Gulf of America, officially runs from June 1 through November 30; the eastern Pacific season runs from May 15 through November 30.

facts.label: Geographic scope
facts.value: The eastern North Pacific basin is the portion of the North Pacific Ocean east of 140°W, while the Atlantic basin includes the Atlantic Ocean, Caribbean Sea, and Gulf of America.

facts.label: Storm classifications
facts.value: A tropical storm has maximum sustained winds of 39–73 mph; a hurricane has maximum sustained winds of at least 74 mph. Major hurricanes are Category 3–5 systems, beginning at 111 mph.

facts.label: Forecasting authority
facts.value: NOAA’s National Hurricane Center in Miami is responsible for tracking tropical cyclones in both the Atlantic and eastern North Pacific and issues operational products including forecasts, public advisories, discussions, and wind-probability information for active cyclones.

facts.label: Naming system
facts.value: Bertha is on the 2026 Atlantic storm-name list. Tropical-cyclone names are assigned from rotating lists maintained through the World Meteorological Organization system.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline follows the July 21–23, 2026 developments involving Bertha’s approach and reported landfall and Fausto’s concurrent eastern-Pacific development; it does not attempt to provide a complete storm lifecycle, full warning record, or final damage and casualty assessment.

event_overview.title: About US History
event_overview.subject: US History
event_overview.summary: This event concerns a July 24, 2026 executive order directing federal officials to place temporary interpretive signage and exhibits on National Park Service-managed approaches to the Smithsonian’s National Museum of American History in Washington, D.C. The order follows a White House review that criticized the museum’s presentation of U.S. history; it is part of a broader administration effort, begun in 2025, to influence historical interpretation at federal sites and Smithsonian institutions.

facts.label: Date and directive
facts.value: President Donald Trump issued the order on July 24, 2026. It directs the Secretary of the Interior, through the National Park Service and in coordination with the White House Domestic Policy office, to install temporary signage along NPS-maintained public sidewalks and walkways leading to the museum.

facts.label: Stated purpose and content
facts.value: The order says the signs are to convey findings from the White House report “Saving America’s Story,” state that museum exhibits should be renovated consistently with that report, and direct visitors to resources the administration describes as accurate information about U.S. history. It also calls for temporary exhibits or signs addressing information the order characterizes as inaccurate, including the treatment of

facts.label: Location
facts.value: The affected museum is the Smithsonian’s National Museum of American History, on the National Mall at Constitution Avenue NW between 12th and 14th Streets in Washington, D.C.

facts.label: Institutional governance
facts.value: The Smithsonian, established by Congress in 1846, is an independent federal trust instrumentality. Its administration is vested in a Board of Regents that includes the Vice President, Chief Justice, six members of Congress, and nine citizen members; it is not an executive-branch agency.

facts.label: Broader policy context
facts.value: The July 2026 order expressly builds on Executive Order 14253 of March 27, 2025, which directed administration officials to pursue the removal of what it called improper ideology from Smithsonian properties and to work with Congress on future Smithsonian appropriations.

event_overview.title: About Netanyahu Arrest Warrant
event_overview.subject: Netanyahu Arrest Warrant
event_overview.summary: The Netanyahu arrest-warrant event concerns an International Criminal Court (ICC) warrant issued for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in the Court’s Situation in the State of Palestine. The warrant has become a focus of debate over the ICC’s jurisdiction, the alleged crimes identified by the Court, and whether national or local authorities can or must act if Netanyahu travels abroad.

facts.label: Warrant date and court
facts.value: ICC Pre-Trial Chamber I issued an arrest warrant for Benjamin Netanyahu on November 21, 2024, in the ICC’s Situation in the State of Palestine.

facts.label: Allegations at the warrant stage
facts.value: The Chamber found reasonable grounds to believe Netanyahu was responsible for alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity, including starvation as a method of warfare, murder, persecution, and other inhumane acts. These are allegations supporting a warrant, not a conviction.

facts.label: Underlying investigation
facts.value: The ICC Prosecutor opened the Situation in Palestine investigation on March 3, 2021; it covers alleged Rome Statute crimes committed since June 13, 2014. The Court had held that its territorial jurisdiction for this situation extends to Gaza and the West Bank, including East Jerusalem.

facts.label: Jurisdiction dispute
facts.value: On November 21, 2024, the same ICC chamber rejected Israel’s then-pending jurisdiction and notification challenges, stating that Israel’s acceptance was not required for the Court to exercise territorial jurisdiction based on Palestine and that the jurisdiction challenge was premature at that stage.

facts.label: Enforcement framework
facts.value: The ICC does not itself carry out arrests; arrest powers rest with states. States Parties to the Rome Statute have obligations to cooperate with ICC arrest-and-surrender requests, while the United States is not a party to the Rome Statute.

event_overview.scope_note: This Muninn timeline follows New York City political and legal statements in July 2026 about possible action on the ICC warrant; it does not attempt to chronicle the full ICC case, the Gaza war, or all international responses to the warrant.

event_overview.title: About Ukraine Conflict
event_overview.subject: Ukraine Conflict
event_overview.summary: The Ukraine conflict is the ongoing armed conflict between Russia and Ukraine, including Russia’s full-scale military operations that began on February 24, 2022. Large-scale long-range missile and drone attacks on Ukrainian cities are a recurring feature of the war and have caused civilian casualties and damage to homes and essential infrastructure.

facts.label: Start of full-scale war
facts.value: The International Court of Justice records that the Russian Federation’s military operations in Ukraine commenced on February 24, 2022.

facts.label: Parties and main location
facts.value: The conflict centers on Ukraine and involves Russian armed forces; UN human-rights monitors also document effects in territory occupied by the Russian Federation and, where information can be verified, impacts in the Russian Federation.

facts.label: Attack pattern
facts.value: Long-range missiles and drones used by Russian armed forces have been a major driver of civilian harm, particularly in urban areas away from the front line; short-range drones are also a major source of casualties near front lines.

facts.label: International monitoring
facts.value: The UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine was deployed in March 2014 and publicly monitors and reports on the human-rights situation, including civilian casualties, across the country.

facts.label: International legal context
facts.value: On March 16, 2022, the International Court of Justice indicated provisional measures ordering Russia to suspend the military operations it had commenced in Ukraine; the order stated that it did not decide the Court’s jurisdiction or the merits of the case.

event_overview.scope_note: This Muninn timeline follows the selected July 19–20, 2026 missile-attack developments and their immediate escalation context, rather than providing a complete chronology of the Russia-Ukraine war or a full accounting of all casualties and strikes.

event_overview.title: About Cockroach Movement Protests
event_overview.subject: Cockroach Movement Protests
event_overview.summary: The Cockroach Movement is a youth-led Indian protest movement organized around the self-styled Cockroach Janta Party (CJP). It began as online satire in May 2026 and developed into street protests focused on alleged examination irregularities, education reform, unemployment and government accountability; supporters have specifically called for the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.

facts.label: Origins and status
facts.value: The CJP emerged online in May 2026 and had become an active, ongoing protest movement by July 21, 2026 rather than a formally established political party or a time-limited event.

facts.label: First major street action
facts.value: Its first reported public street demonstration took place in New Delhi on June 6, 2026, moving the campaign from social media into in-person protest.

facts.label: Organization and participants
facts.value: The movement is associated with the Cockroach Janta Party and its founder, Abhijeet Dipke; it is chiefly youth- and student-led, while later protests also drew professionals and families.

facts.label: Stated aims
facts.value: Its central demands concern accountability for alleged failures in India’s examination system and education reform, including a demand that the education minister resign; the movement also frames unemployment and broader government accountability as concerns.

facts.label: Examination context
facts.value: The protests arose amid controversy over NEET (UG) 2026. The National Testing Agency officially conducted a re-examination on June 21, 2026 and issued fee-refund notices for candidates from the original May 3 examination.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the New Delhi confrontation of July 20, 2026 and protesters’ stated intention to continue on July 21; it does not attempt to catalog the movement’s full online origins, every local protest, or all examination-related proceedings.

event_overview.title: About World Cup 2026
event_overview.subject: World Cup 2026
event_overview.summary: The FIFA World Cup 2026 is the 23rd edition of FIFA’s men’s national-team football championship. It is the first World Cup jointly hosted by Canada, Mexico and the United States, and its expanded field and knockout structure culminate in a final on July 19, 2026.

facts.label: Dates
facts.value: The tournament runs from June 11 through July 19, 2026.

facts.label: Hosts and venues
facts.value: Canada, Mexico and the United States are co-hosting the competition across 16 host cities; this is the first World Cup shared among three countries.

facts.label: Organizer and participants
facts.value: FIFA organizes the tournament, which has a record 48 participating national teams and 104 matches.

facts.label: Competition format
facts.value: The 48 teams are divided into 12 groups of four. The top two in each group and the eight best third-place teams advance to a Round of 32, followed by single-elimination rounds, including a third-place match and final.

facts.label: Concluding matches
facts.value: The third-place match is scheduled for July 18 at Miami Stadium, and the final is scheduled for July 19 at New York New Jersey Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the tournament’s closing-stage developments on July 18-19, 2026, rather than the full qualification process, group stage, or every match in the competition.

events.summary: A large-scale rescue operation is underway in Pengshui County, Chongqing municipality, following a landslide on July 17 that buried part of a residential area. Authorities are working to locate and rescue an unknown number of people trapped under the debris.

revisions.title: Rescue Efforts Underway in China Following Landslide in Chongqing
revisions.summary: A significant landslide occurred in Pengshui County, Chongqing municipality, on July 17, burying part of a residential area. Chinese authorities have initiated a large-scale rescue operation to locate and assist those trapped beneath the debris, although the exact number of individuals affected remains unknown.
